question: Erasmus+ provides not only a European perspective essential for understanding European culture and mutual interdependence, but above all strengthens life experience and knowledge that Europeans can subsequently apply in the labour market. However, insufficient recognition of study results achieved during Erasmus+ mobility remains a systemic problem.

An ESN survey report shows that 42 % of participants were required to change courses during their exchange period and 2.6 % received no credit recognition at all upon return. Thus, students often have to prolong their studies due to nonrecognition of all European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS) credits for completed courses, which may reduce their willingness to participate in mobility programmes.
In this context: 1.
How does the Commission assess the compliance of higher education institutions with the principle of automatic recognition of learning outcomes within Erasmus+?
What measures does the Commission use within Erasmus+ to ensure that Learning Agreements and the ECTS credits earned during mobility are fully and automatically recognised upon return?
Does the Commission intend to take further action to make automatic recognition a uniformly applied practice across Erasmus+ participating institutions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.4.2026) Recognition of credits earned during a study mobility is a cornerstone of the Erasmus+ programme as set out in the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education (ECHE) and reinforced by the Council Recommendation on automatic recognition in 20181.

Moreover, improving the implementation of European Credit accumulation and Transfer System (ECTS) is a key commitment within the European Higher Education Area (EHEA). The Commission monitors the credit recognition at European and national level and published data in the Council Recommendation implementation report2 and the Erasmus+ annual reports3.

The Erasmus+ National Agencies are responsible for the monitoring of the ECHE provisions, including full automatic recognition of student mobility credits, based on the feedback from Erasmus+ students and their higher education institutions.

In case a National Agency detects recurring non-satisfactory recognition rates from an institution holding the ECHE, it can take gradual follow-up measures to oblige this institution to improve their recognition rate. Ultimately, if the institution does not remedy the situation, the National Agency can ask the Commission to withdraw the ECHE from this institution.

In preparing for the next Erasmus+ programme post-2027, the Commission will review the learning agreement and its guidance. The Commission is also chairing the 2027 review of the ECTS Users’ Guide in the context of the EHEA. The aim of this review is to strengthen its implementation, adapt it to current developments and make sure that students can fully benefit from it.
Moreover, the Communication ‘The Union of Skills’4 provides for the development of a common European framework for automatic recognition of, among others, learning periods abroad, by the end of 2027.
